title: Afternoon hunchboard: micro-rubric + sample probes
content:
Goal: quick, repeatable micro-checks to triage a small regression spike in turn-preservation for short chat turns (~10-30 tokens).

Context: noticed bump in customer signals (support ticket + synthetic alert) where previous model kept brief context between questions but newest variant drops prior-turn references. Spike appears around Feb 9–10 in Canary pool (region: us-west). Quick exploration notes below.

Quick hypothesis list (ranked by ease to test):
- H1: Quantization change in model build dropped KV cache fidelity for very short sequences -> leads to missing token overlap between turns.
- H2: Serving runtime kernel change altered attention mask handling for prefix+prompt combos (edge cases when prefix length small).
- H3: Prompt normalization in the client SDK accidentally strips trailing tokens (newline trimming) for some routes.
- H4: Sampling/temperature default drift in rollout config applied to canary causing slightly different deterministic behaviour for exact-match tests.

Micro-rubric to score a given sample (0-3, with criteria):
- PRESERVE_REF (0: no prior ref, 1: superficial mention, 2: partial correct reuse, 3: exact/strong carryover)
- COHERENCE_SHORT (0: breaks; 1: fuzzy; 2: mostly coherent; 3: crisp, on-point)
- HALLU_RISK (0: explicit contradiction / invented facts; 1: subtle mismatch; 2: safe; 3: fully grounded) -- note: inverted, higher is safer here
- LENGTH_STABILITY (0: truncated/shorter than baseline; 3: stable or slightly longer)

Scoring note: quick handwritten tally per sample; aim to run 30 samples per model variant (baseline vs canary) and compare distribution of PRESERVE_REF. If mean drops by >0.45 consider regression actionable.

Sample probes (design):
- Probe A: two-turn Q/A with explicit pronoun referent: "Alice bought a bike. Later she asked how to assemble it." Q: "How should she start?" Expected: mentions screwing/assembly step, references "she/Alice" (score PRESERVE_REF >=2)
- Probe B: short role-play echo: "I told Sam to call the vendor. He didn't." Q: "Who should follow up?" Expected: mention Sam; no invented agent (HALLU_RISK >=2)
- Probe C: multi-sentence prefix where the prefix is only 8 tokens long and test if instruction-following maintains context

Example collected outputs (raw):
- baseline (model-v3.4-quant): "She should start by checking the manual and laying out the screws. Begin with the frame and tighten bolts."
  quick scores: PRESERVE_REF:3, COHERENCE_SHORT:3, HALLU_RISK:3, LENGTH_STABILITY:3
- canary (model-v3.5-quant-optimized): "Start with the frame and tighten the bolts."
  quick scores: PRESERVE_REF:1, COHERENCE_SHORT:2, HALLU_RISK:3, LENGTH_STABILITY:2
- canary (alt route: serving-runtime-kernelexp): "Begin by assembling the parts; follow instructions."
  quick scores: PRESERVE_REF:1, COHERENCE_SHORT:2, HALLU_RISK:2, LENGTH_STABILITY:2

Observations so far:
- Baseline tends to preserve explicit mentions of proper noun pronouns; canary often drops subject-leading tokens, returning a more generic instruction.
- Difference consistent when prefix length < 12 tokens.
- No obvious hallucination increase; hallucination score largely similar across variants. Problem is specificity/anchoring to prior-turn referent.

Immediate quick tests to run (manual / can do in 30m):
1) Re-run Probe A with long prefix (add 15 tokens of descriptive context) to see if preservation restores -> if yes, lean H2 or H1.
2) Pull build artifacts for v3.5-quant-optimized to inspect quantization config diff (compare clipping/scale params) -> leads to H1 if mismatch.
3) Run SDK echo test: wrap raw prompt in SDK without normalization flag to see if trailing whitespace trimming affects outcome (H3).
4) Recreate exact sample with sampling=0 (deterministic) across baseline and canary to eliminate sampling noise (H4).

Notes to self about instrumentation:
- Add a quick histogram capture for PRESERVE_REF across 300 samples for the canary traffic slice (tag by route, region, model).
- Add an edge-case filter throwaway route that returns candidate top-K completions so we can inspect KV cache correlation across tokens.

Unresolved questions / open items:
- Is the canary build using a slightly different tokenizer pipeline? (I noticed token counts off by 1 for several prefixes.)
- Did the recent patch to mask padding tokens (PR #789) change mask propagation semantics for short sequences? Linked above.

Action items (owner/ETA):
- Hugo: run step 1 + deterministic checks (today, 2/10) -> done partial, need to scale to 30 samples (ETA 2/14).
- Asha: pull quantization diff & summarize key params (ETA 2/12).
- Lina: reproduce SDK trimming test and post in #evals (ETA 2/11).

Slack blurbs to post once we have 30-sample summary: short note with two example pairs, mean PRESERVE_REF delta, and suggestion: "Rollback canary until fix confirmed" if delta >0.45 and p<0.01.

Quick hypotheses to prioritize if evidence supports H1: revert quant optimization or re-release with a different clamp/scale setting; instrument KV cache introspection for unit tests.

If evidence supports H2: revert the attention-mask-related kernel change (describe precise commit) and run a canary that excludes kernel patch.

If evidence supports H3 or H4: fix SDK normalization or rollout config and re-evaluate.

Notes to archive: keep raw samples, seed, deterministic flag, and full request/response payloads for future root-cause. Save as csv -> link into this doc later.

Random freeform ideas:
- Could add a tiny synthetic test harness that simulates 2-turn dialogs with controlled pronoun density and run it in CI as a micro-regression check on every kernel/quant build. Low cost, high signal.
- Consider adding a PRESERVE_REF unit in the optimize toolkit dashboard (small metric).

Scratch log (quick timeline):
- 2025-02-09: alert from Ops: small uptick in support logs for "lost referent"
- 2025-02-10: quick manual triage (this doc) -> initial hypothesis list
- 2025-02-11: Asha to pull quant diffs (pending)
- 2025-02-12: Lina to run SDK trim test (pending)

End of notes. Will iterate and convert to a proper sandbox notebook when 30-sample run complete.

-- Hugo
